page: Amazon Web Services m6gd.8xlarge is a general-purpose server powered by the 64-bit ARMv8 architecture. It features 32 dedicated physical cores using AWS Graviton Neoverse-N1 processors running at 2.5 GHz, with one thread per core. The system is equipped with 128.0 GB of system memory, providing 4.0 GB of RAM per core. Storage is bundled with a 1900 GB local NVMe SSD instance store, and the instance operates on the AWS Nitro hypervisor with a baseline network bandwidth of 12 Gbps.

Benchmark data shows average performance across multi-core workloads, including a stress-ng multi-core score of 48563.19 and a Geekbench multi-core score of 11587.0. Memory bandwidth is measured at 1894.51 GB/sec for cached small-block reads and 166.08 GB/sec for uncached large-block reads. However, single-core performance is a notable tradeoff, with Geekbench single-core scoring in the bottom 25% at 950.0 and single-threaded bzip3 decompression falling in the bottom 10% at 7.38 GB/sec.

Given its balanced vCPU-to-RAM ratio and high-capacity local NVMe SSD storage, this server is suited for database operations, static web serving, and multi-threaded software compilation. Passmark database operations score at an average level of 20452.11, and Redis SET operations reach 36.57 million operations per second. The ARM64 architecture and dedicated core allocation offer resource density and qualitative cost efficiency for multi-threaded workloads, though it is less optimal for single-threaded tasks or large-scale LLM text generation.
